```{=html}
<a class="skip" href="#main-content">Skip to content</a><header class="site-nav"><a class="brand" href="../index.html" aria-label="GLOBE home"><img src="../assets/images/globe-logo-transparent.png" alt="GLOBE" width="2172" height="724"></a><button class="menu-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="main-nav">Menu</button><nav class="nav-links" id="main-nav" aria-label="Main navigation"><a href="../index.html">Home</a><a href="../pages/about.html" aria-current="page">Project</a><a href="../pages/network.html">Network</a><a href="../pages/monitoring.html">Monitoring</a><a href="../pages/join.html">Join</a></nav></header><div id="main-content"><section class="page-intro"><p class="eyebrow">ABOUT GLOBE</p><h1>An initiative across oceans.</h1><p>GLOBE focuses on <i>Vibrio</i> dynamics during extreme El Niño events, within the wider context of marine microbial responses to a warming ocean.</p></section><section class="wrap prose"><p><a href="research.html">Explore the research questions ↗</a></p><h2>Scientific scope</h2><p>El Niño alters oceanographic conditions, with effects that vary among regions. GLOBE investigates whether these changing conditions favour the introduction and expansion of pathogenic <i>Vibrio</i> lineages, while examining changes in microbial community composition and functional potential.</p><p>The initial initiative includes 30 coastal sampling stations in 23 countries, across the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian oceans and the Mediterranean Sea.</p><h2>Observations before and during El Niño</h2><p>The project description specifies monthly sampling, increasing to fortnightly sampling as the El Niño front arrives. Seawater microbes, phytoplankton and zooplankton are considered alongside environmental measurements. Metagenomic sequencing and analysis of <i>Vibrio</i> isolates support comparisons before and during the event.</p><h2>An open network of scientists</h2><p>GLOBE is a free and independent international network of scientists. Researchers can propose coordinated sampling across this worldwide network in response to exceptional ocean events, including El Niño. Participation and new collaborations are welcome; each campaign is developed with the participating teams and agreed local sampling capacity.</p><h2>International identity</h2><p>GLOBE is an independent international scientific collaboration. Participating national networks, including the Italian Omics Observatory Network, contribute to the shared initiative.</p><h2>Coordination and participation</h2><p>Project coordinators, institutional affiliations, funding acknowledgements and partner contacts will be listed after confirmation. No names or affiliations have been inferred.</p></section></div><footer class="site-footer"><div><strong>GLOBE</strong><p><i>Vibrio</i> dynamics and ocean microbiome research.<br>International collaboration across a changing ocean.</p></div><p>Project scope: 30 coastal stations · 23 countries<br><a href="../pages/news.html">News</a> · <a href="../pages/resources.html">Sources & resources</a> · <a href="../pages/privacy.html">Privacy & data use</a> · <a href="../pages/members.html">Partner workspace</a><br>Independent international scientific collaboration</p></footer><script src="../assets/js/site.js"></script>
```
